title: The full test run passes every time, not one run in two
goal: Three video and title tests fail at random when the whole test suite runs and pass when run on their own, so a loop task can be refused its commit by a test that has nothing to do with its change. Make them hold up under the full run's load.
notes: Seen 2026-10-13 by the runner on size-mode-measures-real-buttons-and-objects-not, four full runs of `Scripts/test.sh` on a quiet machine (no process over 50% CPU), code unrelated to these tests: run 1 failed 3 issues; run 2 failed `TitleSetFramesTests.swift:214` (median 17.72 ms vs < 16) and `GrainBandingExportTests.swift:106` ((grainy * 3 → 93) <= (plain * 2 → 88)); run 3 failed `VideoCutExportTests.swift:69` (.readerGaveUp("no picture came out of the recording for 30 seconds")); run 4 passed all 12871. `Scripts/test.sh --filter "VideoCutExportTests|TitleSetFramesTests|GrainBandingExportTests"` passed 10/10 alone each time. The title-frame one is a wall-clock budget, not a ratio against a ruler like the PerfClock/CPUYardstick checks.
acceptance: Four full runs of Scripts/test.sh in a row on an otherwise quiet machine pass with no failures
The title-frame time check, the grain banding check and the cut export check still fail when what they guard really regresses (say how this was shown)
Nothing is skipped or loosened without a comment saying what was measured

Seen again 2026-10-13 by the runner on measurements-are-named-for-their-mode-and-every (load average 16-20 from other sessions): full run 1 failed Space3DPerfTests:118 (median 25.9 ms), TitleSetFramesTests:214 (17.6 ms), TextDepthPerspectiveTests:170 (24.4 ms), DepthTransitionRenderTests:138 (49.6 ms), TextRevealRenderTests:220 (21-43 ms); full run 2 failed only GrainBandingExportTests:106 (93 <= 88). So the wall-clock budgets also trip under load from OTHER sessions, not just the suite's own parallelism.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Reproduced, frame gates: with a second process keeping the GPU busy (/tmp/flaky/gpuburn, 4 threads of Core Image blur, self-ending), Scripts/test.sh --filter of the seven frame suites failed 5 issues (text flip 149.5ms vs 77, 2.5D 153.7 vs 64, scrub 80.1 vs 74...). AND on a quiet machine the same seven suites run together failed 2 (2.5D 42.5ms vs 24, flip 41.8 vs 29) though each alone reads 5.4 and 7.6ms. Cause 1: every DocumentRenderer() shares one process-wide CIContext, so a timed frame queues behind the other render suites (the ruler on its own context read normal 3.4ms beside a 36ms subject). Cause 2: the filter-graph yardstick does not track a busy GPU's effect on a frame (2.77x vs up to 12x). 12 CPU-only burners changed nothing (frames are GPU-bound).

Fix, frame gates: MachineSpeed.timedRenderer() (DocumentRenderer(privateContext:), the icon strip's existing fix) + MachineSpeed.checkFrames (interleaved, new .frame yardstick: ten small layers on a 1080p ground rendered to a bitmap, 3.3ms calibrated). Ruler chosen by measurement (temp scratch test, deleted): flip/frame ratio 1.68 idle, 1.54-1.70 loaded; flip/filterGraph 1.29 -> 2.06. Moved: TitleSetPerfTests, TextDepthPerspective perf, MotionBlur insideAFrame, DepthTransition perf (now per kind), Space3DPerf, TextReveal twelveWords, ScrubCompositePerf. Budgets unchanged (baseline x2.5 + 8ms). Under 4-thread GPU load the flip read 58ms raw, 10.3 normalized vs 28: pass.

Regressions still caught: temp mutant in DocumentRenderer.renderLocked rendering every frame 10x -> 17 issues across 6 of 7 suites quiet (flip read 27.7 vs 28, just under), 19 issues under 2-thread GPU load, none excused as untrusted. A 4x render mutant (2-3x frame cost) passes, as it would have under the 2026-10-13 budgets on a quiet machine: those budgets only catch >3x by design (MachineSpeed.jitterSlackMS). Mutant reverted.

Grain banding: alone 6/6 identical (plain 48, grain 24). Beside other encoders (Scripts/test.sh --filter PhotonzMediaTests) the encoder writes different files: plain 4 KB -> 86 KB, 48 -> 44 rows; and one grainy frame reads 11 to 32 rows, so the single read at 0.3s gave 14/24/26/31; reproduced the exact failure (plain 44, grain 31, 93 <= 88). Fix: median over all 18 frames, and the line at 3/4 of plain instead of 2/3, measured: default grain 0.50 quiet, 0.68 under CPU+GPU stress beside other encoders (30 vs 44); amount 20 0.56, 16 0.83, 12 1.0, 8 1.0 (mutant amount 8 fails: 144 <= 96). Faster blue-channel extraction keeps it at 7.6s.

VideoCutExport readerGaveUp (30s with no frame, seen once 2026-10-13): NOT reproduced in 12 runs that include it (6 full suites, one with 12 CPU burners; 4 PhotonzMediaTests runs, one with 12 CPU burners + 4-thread GPU burner; 2 more media runs). Exporter and its 30s limit left as they are; nothing loosened. Not filed separately: this task's notes carry the one sighting, and the 2026-10-02 hang task (done) covers the guard. If it shows again, sample the helper during the stall.
Acceptance: four full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row passed, 13101 tests each (352s, 326s, 327s, 325s); closest frame gate used 40% of its budget; grain read 24-26 against plain 44-48.
